label: thm:main phi4
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main phi4}
For every $L\geq1$ and $m,\lambda>0$, consider the
$\Phi^4_2$ model or the sine-Gordon model with fixed
$\beta^2<2\pi$ on $\mathbb T_L^2$.
Fix $\sigma_p\geq\sigma>0$ such that
\eqref{eq:lsi-lattice} and~\eqref{eq:poincare-lattice}
hold uniformly in $\delta$.

There exist finite constants $C>0$ and
$R=R(m,\lambda,\sigma)$, with $C$ universal and $R$
possibly depending on $L$ only through $\sigma$, such that
for every $\gamma>0$, $t\geq0$, and
$f\in L^2(\mu\otimes\kappa)$ with
$\|f\|_{L^2(\mu\otimes\kappa)}=1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-convergence}
\left\|P_t f-\int f\mathop{}\!\mathrm d(\mu\otimes\kappa)\right\|_{L^2(\mu\otimes\kappa)}
\leq C\exp\left(
-\frac{\sigma_p\gamma t}
{C(\sqrt{\sigma_p}+R+\gamma)^2}
\right).
\end{equation}
Moreover, for the $\Phi^4_2$ model and every
$\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant
$C_{L,\varepsilon}>0$ such that the estimate
\eqref{eq:main-convergence} also holds with
$R\leq C_{L,\varepsilon}m$, for all
$0<m\leq1$ and
$0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0(m)\wedge m^{4+\varepsilon}$.
head: environment
name: Equilibration of dynamics

label: remark:comparison
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark:comparison}
The lattice log-Sobolev and Poincar\'e inequalities pass to the
continuum limit, so that $\sigma$ and $\sigma_p$ are also
admissible constants for the corresponding inequalities under
$\mu$. Denoting by $\sigma_p^{\mathrm{opt}}(\mu)$ the optimal
Poincar\'e constant of $\mu$, we thus have
$\sigma_p^{\mathrm{opt}}(\mu)\geq\sigma_p\geq\sigma$.
For the $\Phi^4_2$ model in the weak-coupling regime of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main phi4}, the susceptibility estimates of
Bauerschmidt and Dagallier~\cite{bauerschmidt_logsobolev_2024}
give $\sigma_p^{\mathrm{opt}}(\mu)\lesssim m^2$,
uniformly in $L$, by testing the Poincar\'e inequality with
the spatial average of the field. Since one may choose
$\sigma_p=\sigma\gtrsim m^2$, it follows that
$\sigma_p^{\mathrm{opt}}(\mu) \simeq m^2$.
Together with the bound $R\leq C_{L,\varepsilon}m$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:main phi4} then yields a kinetic relaxation
rate of at least
\begin{equation}
\frac{m^2\gamma}{C_{L,\varepsilon}(m+\gamma)^2}.
\end{equation}
Choosing $\gamma=m$ yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least
order $m$, compared with the optimal overdamped relaxation rate
$\sigma_p^{\mathrm{opt}}(\mu) \simeq m^2$. 
This establishes the announced acceleration in the small-mass regime.
head: environment

label: rem:regular-one-dimensional
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:regular-one-dimensional}
In one spatial dimension, analogous $L^2$ convergence estimates
follow from the dimension-free result of Cao, Lu, and
Wang~\cite{cao_explicit_2023}. For a smooth, bounded-below
interaction potential $V$ satisfying suitable growth conditions
and $\operatorname{Hess} V\geq-R^2$, their result yields, provided the
corresponding lattice Gibbs measures satisfy a uniform
Poincar\'e inequality with constant $\sigma_p>0$,
a relaxation rate
\[
\alpha\geq
\frac{\sigma_p\gamma}
{C(\sqrt{\sigma_p}+R+\gamma)^2},
\]
uniformly in the lattice discretization.
The corresponding continuum estimate follows by passing
to the limit as in~\cite{LATTICE}.
head: environment

label: ass:log-sobolev
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:log-sobolev}
There exist constants $\sigma_p\geq\sigma>0$, independent
of $\delta$, such that the measures $\mu_\delta$ satisfy
the log-Sobolev inequality~\eqref{eq:lsi-lattice} and the
Poincar\'e inequality~\eqref{eq:poincare-lattice}.
head: environment

label: ass:hessian finite
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:hessian finite}
For every $\delta$, the interaction potential
$V_\delta$ belongs to $C^2(\mathbb R)$.
There exists a finite constant $R\geq0$, independent of
$\delta$, such that
\[
\log\int
\exp\left(\frac{4}{\sigma}Q_\delta(u)\right)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu_\delta(u)
\leq\frac{4R^2}{\sigma},
\]
where $Q_\delta(u)=-\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess} U(u))$ is the
negative of the lowest eigenvalue of $\operatorname{Hess} U(u)$,
and $\sigma$ is as in Assumption~\ref{ass:log-sobolev}.
head: environment
name: Simple version

label: ass:potential-intro
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:potential-intro}
For every $\delta$, the interaction potential
$V_\delta$ belongs to $C^2(\mathbb R)$.
There exist functions
$Q_{\delta,i}:\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}\to\mathbb R$,
indexed by $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, and a finite constant $R\geq0$,
independent of $\delta$ and $L$ except through $\sigma$,
such that for every $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, $u\in\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}$,
and $h\in\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}$ supported in $B(i,2)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:assumption on hessian}
\delta^d\sum_{x\in\Lambda_\delta}
\left[
\bigl(V_\delta''(u(x))+m^2\bigr)h(x)^2
+\frac12|\nabla_\delta h(x)|^2
\right]
\geq -Q_{\delta,i}(u)\|h\|_{L^2(\Lambda_\delta)}^2,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:potential assumption exponential}
\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}
\log\int
\exp\left(\frac{4}{\sigma}Q_{\delta,i}(u)\right)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu_\delta(u)
\leq\frac{4R^2}{\sigma},
\end{equation}
where $\sigma$ is as in Assumption~\ref{ass:log-sobolev}.
head: environment
name: Uniform version

label: thm:decay of variance
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:decay of variance}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:log-sobolev} and either
Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite} or~\ref{ass:potential-intro}, together with
the technical Assumption~\ref{ass:technical} stated
in Section~\ref{sec:clw}, there exists a universal
finite constant $C>0$ such that for every
$\delta>0$ with $L/\delta\in\mathbb N$,
$\tilde\gamma>0$, $t'\geq0$, and
$f\in L^2(\mu_\delta\otimes\kappa_\delta)$,
\[
\left\|P_{t'}^\delta f-\int f\mathop{}\!\mathrm d(\mu_\delta\otimes\kappa_\delta)\right\|_{L^2(\mu_\delta\otimes\kappa_\delta)}
\leq C e^{-\alpha_\delta t'}
\left\|f-\int f\mathop{}\!\mathrm d(\mu_\delta\otimes\kappa_\delta)\right\|_{L^2(\mu_\delta\otimes\kappa_\delta)},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_\delta=
\frac{\sigma_p\delta^d\tilde\gamma}
{C\bigl[\delta^{d/2}(\sqrt{\sigma_p}+\tilde R)
+\tilde\gamma\bigr]^2},
\]
with $\tilde R=R$ under Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite}
and $\tilde R=\sqrt{R^2+C_d}$ under
Assumption~\ref{ass:potential-intro},
where $C_d$ only depends on the dimension of the lattice~$\Lambda$.
head: environment
name: Lattice hypocoercivity

label: thm:integrability
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:integrability}
Let $d=2$, and consider the lattice $\Phi^4_2$ model or
the lattice sine-Gordon model with fixed $0<\beta^2<4\pi$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every $L\geq1$, $m,\lambda>0$, and
$\delta>0$ with $L/\delta\in\mathbb N$, there exist functions
$Q_{\delta,i}:\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}\to\mathbb R$,
indexed by $i\in\mathbb Z^2$, such that for every
$i\in\mathbb Z^2$, $u\in\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}$,
$h\in\mathbb R^{\Lambda_\delta}$ supported in $B(i,2)$,
and $q>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:integrability bounds}
\begin{split}
\delta^2\sum_{x\in\Lambda_\delta}
\left[
\bigl(V_\delta''(u(x))+m^2\bigr)h(x)^2
+\frac12|\nabla_\delta h(x)|^2
\right]
&\geq
-Q_{\delta,i}(u)\|h\|_{L^2(\Lambda_\delta)}^2,\\
\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^2}\log\int
\exp\bigl(qQ_{\delta,i}(u)\bigr)\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu_\delta(u)
&\leq \mathcal R(q,m,\lambda),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal R(q,m,\lambda)<\infty$ is independent
of $\delta$ and $L$.

\item[(ii)] For the lattice $\Phi^4_2$ model, let
$Q_\delta(u)=-\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess} U(u))$,
as in Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite}.
There exists a universal constant $c_0>0$ such that
for every $L\geq1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a
constant $C_{L,\varepsilon}<\infty$ with the following
property: for all $0<m\leq1$ and
$0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0(m)\wedge m^{4+\varepsilon}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:global spectral estimate phi4}
\sup_{\substack{\delta>0\\L/\delta\in\mathbb N}}
\log\int
\exp\left(\frac{4}{c_0m^2}Q_\delta(u)\right)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu_\delta(u)
\leq C_{L,\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Spectral estimates in two dimensions

title: Proof
body_md:
Item~(i) is proved in Section~\ref{sec:measures}.
Item~(ii) follows immediately, since the additional $\tfrac 1 2 |\nabla_\delta h|^2$ term
only improves the estimates.
head: environment

label: rem:global-spectral-estimate
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:global-spectral-estimate}
The global estimate in Theorem~\ref{thm:integrability}(ii)
verifies Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite} with
$R=O(m)$ at fixed volume.
Indeed, in the weak-coupling regime under consideration,
$\sigma_*=c_0m^2$ is an admissible log-Sobolev constant,
uniformly in $\delta$.
By~\eqref{eq:global spectral estimate phi4},
Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite} therefore holds with
\[
R^2=\frac{\sigma_*}{4}C_{L,\varepsilon}
=\frac{c_0C_{L,\varepsilon}}{4}m^2.
\]
This is the bound needed to establish the small-mass
acceleration discussed in Remark~\ref{remark:comparison}.
head: environment

label: thm:3 dimensions
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:3 dimensions}
Let $d=3$ and $L=1$. For every $m,\lambda>0$ and
$\delta>0$ with $1/\delta\in\mathbb N$, consider the
lattice $\Phi^4_3$ model with interaction
$
V_\delta(u)=\lambda\mathord{\mathopen: u^4 \mathclose:}
+\lambda^2a_\delta\mathord{\mathopen: u^2 \mathclose:}.
$
Let $Q_\delta(u)=-\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess} U(u))$, so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:global hessian phi3}
Q_\delta(u)=
-\inf_{\|\psi\|_{L^2(\Lambda_\delta)}=1}
\delta^3\sum_{x\in\Lambda_\delta}
\left[
\bigl(V_\delta''(u(x))+m^2\bigr)\psi(x)^2
+|\nabla_\delta\psi(x)|^2
\right].
\end{equation}
For every $q>0$,
\[
\log\int\exp\bigl(qQ_\delta(u)\bigr)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu_\delta(u)
\leq \mathcal R(q,m,\lambda),
\]
where $\mathcal R(q,m,\lambda)<\infty$ is independent
of $\delta$.
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{\substack{
0<m\leq1,\ 0<\lambda\leq m^{3}\\
0<q\leq m^{-2}
}}
\mathcal R(q,m,\lambda)<\infty.
\]
head: environment
name: Spectral estimate in three dimensions

title: Proof
body_md: Section~\ref{sec:phi43}.
head: environment

label: rem:bottom-spectrum
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:bottom-spectrum}
The functions $Q_{\delta,i}$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:integrability}(i) can be chosen as
negatives of the lowest eigenvalues of modified discrete
Schr\"odinger operators with localized potentials.
By contrast, $-Q_\delta$ in
Theorems~\ref{thm:integrability}(ii)
and~\ref{thm:3 dimensions} is the lowest eigenvalue
of $\operatorname{Hess} U$.
These results thus provide exponential lower-tail
estimates for the spectra of singular random
Schr\"odinger operators.

In the $\Phi^4_3$ model, the potential $V_\delta''(u)$
is non-Gaussian and renormalized, with spatial regularity
analogous to that of two-dimensional white noise.
Its spectral analysis is therefore closely related
to that of the Anderson Hamiltonian; see
\cite{allez_continuous_2015,gubinelli_semilinear_2020,
labbe_continuous_2019}.
For the white-noise Anderson Hamiltonian, exponential
lower-tail estimates for the lowest eigenvalue are known;
see~\cite{allez_continuous_2015,labbe_continuous_2019}.
To our knowledge, such estimates have not previously been established for the non-Gaussian, renormalized potential considered here. They may be of independent interest.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
To obtain convergence estimates uniform also in the volume
for the $\Phi^4_3$ model, one would need to use the
localized criterion of
Assumption~\ref{ass:potential-intro}.
This requires retaining only half of the gradient term,
as in~\eqref{eq:assumption on hessian}.
However, the renormalization counterterm in $V_\delta''$
is tuned to the full Laplacian in $\operatorname{Hess} U$.
Reducing its coefficient changes the required
renormalization, so the cancellation of divergences
is lost.
It would therefore be interesting to develop a refinement
of Theorem~\ref{thm:decay of variance} that yields
volume-uniform estimates without modifying the
renormalized Hessian.
head: environment

label: thm:lattice-convergence
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:lattice-convergence}
Let $d=2$ and $L\geq1$, and consider either the
$\Phi^4_2$ model or the sine-Gordon model with
$0<\beta^2<2\pi$.
Let $(u,\partial_tu)$ and
$(u_\delta,\partial_tu_\delta)$ be the corresponding
stationary continuum and lattice solutions of
\eqref{eq:sdnlw continuum} and
\eqref{eq:sdnlw lattice}, constructed on a common
probability space.
For every $T>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the following
hold almost surely as $\delta\to0$:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$\mathcal{\tilde E} u_\delta\to u$ in
$C([0,T],H^{-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T_L^2))$;
\item
$\mathcal{\tilde E}\partial_tu_\delta\to\partial_tu$ in
$C([0,T],H^{-1-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T_L^2))$.
\end{itemize}

label: thm:ngs bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:ngs bound}
Assume that the measure $\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with constant $\sigma$.
Let $\psi \colon \mathbb R^\Lambda \to \mathbb R$ be a continuous function such that
\[
\int \exp\left( \frac{2}{\sigma} \psi(u) \right) \mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu(u) \leq K
\]
for some $K > 0$.
Then for any $f \in C^\infty_b(\mathbb R^\Lambda)$ we have the estimate
\[
\delta^d \int \psi(u) |f(u)|^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu(u)
\leq \frac{\sigma \delta^d}{2} \log(K) \int |f(u)|^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu(u)
    + \int |\nabla f(u)|^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu(u).
\]

label: thm:clw 2.3
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:clw 2.3}
Let $g \in H^2(\tau \otimes \mu_\delta)$ be such that
$(\partial_t g, \nabla_u g) \in H^1_0(\tau \otimes \mu_\delta)^{1 + |\Lambda|}$.
Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
\|D^2 g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2
\leq 2\|(-\partial_{tt} + \nabla_u^\ast \nabla_u) g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2
    + 2(R^2+2^d) \delta^d \|\nabla_u g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2, \text{ and}\\
\|\nabla_u^2 g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2
\leq 2\|\nabla_u^\ast \nabla_u g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2
    + 2(R^2+2^d) \delta^d \|\nabla_u g\|_{L^2(\tau \otimes \mu)}^2.
\end{gathered}
\]
Here $D^2$ is the Hessian with respect to all of
$t$ and $u(x)$, $x \in \Lambda$.
If  Assumption~\ref{ass:hessian finite} holds,
then the above bounds hold with $R^2+2^d$ replaced by $R^2$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Our Assumption~\ref{ass:log-sobolev} is stronger than the
Poincaré inequality assumed in~\cite{cao_explicit_2023}.
This is discussed in Lemma~\ref{thm:clw 2.1},
which replaces~\cite[Lemma~2.1]{cao_explicit_2023}.
We use the NGS~bound in our Lemma~\ref{thm:clw 2.3},
which replaces~\cite[Lemma~2.3]{cao_explicit_2023}.

The only remaining dimension dependency is in~\cite[Lemma~2.2]{cao_explicit_2023},
which uses Item~1 of Assumption~\ref{ass:technical}.
With our proof of Lemma~\ref{thm:clw 2.3} this technical result is only used in
qualitative way at the end of~\cite[Lemma~2.4]{cao_explicit_2023}.
Therefore these modifications already suffice to make the proof uniform in $\delta > 0$.

In~\cite{cao_explicit_2023} $f_0$ is assumed to be in~$L^2(\mu;\, H^1_\kappa)$,
but since the inequality is stated in terms of $L^2$ norm,
we can argue by density that the result holds also for $f_0 \in L^2(\mu \otimes \kappa)$.

label: thm:boue-dupuis
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:boue-dupuis}
If $F \colon \mathbb R^{\Lambda} \to \mathbb R$ is continuous and bounded below,
then
\[
\begin{split}
-\log \int \exp(-F(u)) \mathop{}\!\mathrm d \nu_{\delta}(u)
&= \inf_{h \in \mathbb H_{a}} \mathord{\mathbb E}_{\mathbb{P}} \left[
    F(W + I[h]) + \frac 1 2 \int_0^1 \|h_s\|_{L^2}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm d s
    \right]\\
&= \min_{\zeta \in \overline{\mathcal X}} \mathord{\mathbb E}_\zeta \left[
    F(W + I[h]) + \frac 1 2 \int_0^1 \|h_s\|_{L^2}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm d s
    \right].
\end{split}
\]

Assume $V \in C^3(\mathbb R)$.
For any $\delta > 0$, we have

-\partial_{u(x)} Q(u) = \chi(x) V'''(u(x))(\psi^u(x))^2,

\[

    \sum_{x \in\Lambda}
    \left(\chi V''(u)\psi^2
    +m^2\psi^2+ \frac 1 2 |\nabla_\delta \psi|^2\right).
\]

\label{prop:coupling}
Let $\mu_{\beta}$ be the lattice sine-Gordon measure for $\beta^2 < 4 \pi$,
and $\rho$ a weight as in Section~\ref{sec:phi42 measure}.

    + \frac{C \lambda^2}{m^2} \exp \!\left( \frac{C \lambda}{m^2} \right)$.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\nu^{qQ}=e^{qQ}\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mu/Z^{qQ}$, we have
\[
\int e^{-qQ(u)}\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\nu^{qQ}(u)=\frac{1}{Z^{qQ}}.
\]
Jensen's inequality therefore gives
\[
-\int qQ(u)\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\nu^{qQ}(u)
\leq \log\int e^{-qQ(u)}\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\nu^{qQ}(u)
=-\log Z^{qQ},
\]
which is the claimed bound.

label: prop-gub-hov
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop-gub-hov}
Let $u = W + W^{[3]} + K$, where $W$ and $W^{[3]}$ are the
stationary solutions to
\[
(\partial_t+m^2-\operatorname{\mathrm{\Delta}}_\delta)W
    =\sqrt2 \, \mathrm P_{\geq1}\xi, \qquad
(\partial_t+m^2-\operatorname{\mathrm{\Delta}}_\delta)W^{[3]}
    =-4\lambda\mathord{\mathopen: W^3 \mathclose:}.
\]
and $K$ is a stationary process. Then
\[
\mathord{\mathbb E} \left[ \delta^3 \sum_{x \in \Lambda}
    \big((m^2-\operatorname{\mathrm{\Delta}}_\delta)K
    +4\lambda\bigl(\mathord{\mathopen: u^3 \mathclose:}-\mathord{\mathopen: W^3 \mathclose:}\bigr)
    +2\lambda^2a_{\delta}u\big)K \right]
\geq \mathord{\mathbb E} \mathcal{E} (K) - \mathord{\mathbb E} \mathcal{B}^3 (W, \lambda, m).
\]
where $\mathcal{B}^3 (W, \lambda, m)$ is a stochastic term that satisfies
\[
\mathord{\mathbb E} |\mathcal{B}^3 (W, \lambda, m)| \leq p (\lambda, m)
\]
where $p (\lambda, m)$ is a rational function of $\lambda$ and $m$ such that
$|p (\lambda, m)| \leq C$ as long as $\lambda \leq m^2 \leq 1$.

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows as Lemma~4.4 and Theorem~4.5 from~\cite{gubinelli_pde_2021},
with minor modifications to obtain the required behaviour in $\lambda$, $m$,
and setting the weight $\rho = 1$, as we are on a torus of fixed volume.

title: Remark
body_md:
We have excluded the zero mode of~$\xi$ from~$W$ to make sure that
$m^2 - \operatorname{\mathrm{\Delta}}_\delta$ has a spectral gap uniformly in~$m$.
This will make the bounds on stochastic terms built from $W$ independent of~$m$.
The price to pay is that we will have to include the corresponding zero mode term into~$K$,
however this will not present any significant problems.

body_md:
\label{3d-form-wick-square}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, there exists a family of random variables $\Xi_{\delta}>0$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item for every $p<\infty$, we have $ \sup_{\delta>0}\mathord{\mathbb E}[\Xi_{\delta}^p]\leq C_p$; and
\item for every $\varphi$ with $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(\Lambda)} = 1$, we have

    \mathcal {A}_\delta(W)(\varphi)
    \geq (1-\lambda/2)
        \|\varphi\|_{H^{1-\varepsilon}(\Lambda)}^2
        -C_\varepsilon \lambda^{1-2\varepsilon}\Xi_{\delta}-1.

\end{itemize}

\label{first-commutator}
Let
\[
\mathfrak{C}_1 (\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}, \varphi)
\coloneqq \langle \mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:} \prec \varphi, \varphi \rangle_{L^2 (\Lambda)}
    + \langle \mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:} \circ \varphi, \varphi \rangle_{L^2 (\Lambda)}
    - \langle \mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:} \succ \varphi, \varphi \rangle_{L^2 (\Lambda)}.
\]
The following estimate holds for $\varphi \in H^{1 - \varepsilon}$
satisfying $\|\varphi\|_{L^2} \leq 1$:
\[
|\mathfrak{C}_1 (\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}, \varphi)|
\lesssim (1 + \|\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{- 1 - \varepsilon}})
    \|\varphi\|^{1 + 4 \varepsilon}_{H^{1 - \varepsilon}}.
\]

title: Remark
body_md:
If we had applied the Boué--Dupuis formula in this setting to deduce exponential tails,
we could conclude with the above lemma as well as the considerations from~\cite{barashkov_variational_2020}.
However this would require to adapt the stochastic estimates in~\cite{barashkov_variational_2020} to the lattice setting,
which is why we opt to use the SPDE-based method where most of the required estimates have already been established.

Since the gradient of $Q(u)$ appears in the method we employ,
we are obliged to deduce some estimates on the ground state before we can proceed.
This will be carried out in the following.

label: lem:competitor
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:competitor}
There exists $\varphi \in L^2 (\Lambda)$ such that
\[
\|\varphi\|_{\mathcal C^{1 - \varepsilon}}
    \leq C(1+\|\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{-1-\varepsilon}}^p),
\qquad \|\varphi\|_{L^2} = 1,
\]
and $p < \infty$ such that
\[
|\mathcal A(W)(\varphi)|
\leq C\left(1+\|W^{2\diamond2}\|_{\mathcal C^{-\varepsilon}}
    + \|\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{-1-\varepsilon}}\right)^p.
\]

label: bound-3d-ground
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{bound-3d-ground}
Let $\psi^{W + I}$ minimize $\mathcal{A} (W + W^{[3]}+ K) (\psi)$
over $\{\psi \colon \|\psi\|_{L^2}=1\}$.
Then, for every $\eta \in (0, 1)$ and $\lambda>0$,
\[
\|\psi^{W + I}\|^2_{H^{1 - \varepsilon}}
\leq \eta \mathcal{E}(K) + \mathcal{B}^2_{\eta} (W, \lambda, m),
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal B^2_{\eta}(W,\lambda,m)
&= \frac{C}{\eta} \Bigl( 1
    + \|\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{-1-\varepsilon}}
    + \|W^{2\diamond2}\|_{\mathcal C^{-\varepsilon}}\\
&\qquad\qquad + \|WW^{[3]}\|_{\mathcal C^{-1/2-\varepsilon}}
    + \|W\|_{\mathcal C^{-1/2-\varepsilon}}^2
    + \|W^{[3]}\|_{L^2}^2 \Bigr)^p\\
&\qquad +\mathcal B^1(W,\lambda,m, 16/\eta)
\end{split}
\]
for $p$ sufficiently large.

title: Remark

The product $W W^{[3]}$ does not possess enough regularity to be well-defined
in a deterministic way in the $\delta \rightarrow 0$ limit.
However one can show, as for example in~\cite[Section~4]{gubinelli_pde_2021}, that
$\sup_{\delta} \mathord{\mathbb E} \|W W^{[3]}\|^p_{\mathcal C^{- 1 / 2 - \varepsilon}} < \infty$
for any $p < \infty$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\{ \Delta_j \}_{j = -1, \ldots, j_\Lambda}$ be the Littlewood--Paley blocks
as in~\cite[Definition~2.17]{martin_paracontrolled_2019}.
The weighted Besov space $B^s_{p,r}(\rho)$ on $\Lambda$ is defined
as the completion of~$C^\infty_c(\Lambda)$ with respect to the norm
\[
\|f\|_{B^s_{p,r}(\rho)}
\coloneqq \left\|2^{js} \|\rho \Delta_j f\|_{L^p(\Lambda)}\right\|_{\ell^r(j)}.
\]
On $\mathbb T^d$ and $\mathbb R^d$ the definition is analogous.
We abbreviate $H^s \coloneqq B^s_{2,2}$ and $\mathcal C^s \coloneqq B^s_{\infty, \infty}$.
head: environment
name: Besov spaces

label: thm:besov properties
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:besov properties}
Let the ambient space be either~$\Lambda_\delta$ or~$\mathbb T^2$,
let $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ be weights,
let $p = 1/p_1 + 1/p_2$ and $r = 1/r_1 + 1/r_2$ be Hölder conjugate pairs in~$[1,\infty]$,
and let $s \in \mathbb R$.
Then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\renewcommand{(\alph{enumi})}{(\alph{enumi})}
\item Multiplication: $\|fg\|_{B^s_{p,r}(\rho_1 \rho_2)}
\lesssim \|f\|_{B^s_{p_1, r}(\rho_1)} \|g\|_{B^t_{p_2, r}(\rho_2)}$
    for $t \geq s$ such that $s + t > 0$.
\item Duality: $\|\rho_1 \rho_2 fg\|_{L^1}
        \lesssim \|f\|_{B^{-s}_{p_1, r_1}(\rho_1)} \|g\|_{B^s_{p_2, r_2}(\rho_2)}$,
    where we set $p = r = 1$.
\item Interpolation: let $\theta \in (0,1)$ and
    \[
        s = \theta s_1 + (1-\theta) s_2, \quad
        \frac 1 p = \frac{\theta}{p_1} + \frac{1-\theta}{p_2}, \quad
        \frac 1 r = \frac{\theta}{r_1} + \frac{1-\theta}{r_2}.
    \]
    Then $\|f\|_{B^s_{p,r}(\rho_1^{\theta} \rho_2^{1-\theta})}
        \leq \|f\|_{B^{s_1}_{p_1, r_1}(\rho_1)}^\theta
            \|f\|_{B^{s_2}_{p_2, r_2}(\rho_2)}^{1-\theta}$.
\item Besov embedding: $\|f\|_{B^s_{p,r}(\rho_1)} \lesssim \|f\|_{B^t_{q,r}(\rho_1)}$
    where $q < p$ and $t \geq s + d(1/q - 1/p)$.
\item $L^p$ embedding: $\|f\|_{B^0_{p,\infty}(\rho_1)} \lesssim \|f\|_{L^p(\rho_1)}$.
\item Second parameter tradeoff:
    $\|f\|_{B^s_{p,r}(\rho_1)} \lesssim \|f\|_{B^{s+\varepsilon}_{p,\infty}(\rho_1)}$
    for all $1 \leq r \leq \infty$ and $\varepsilon > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
The implicit constants are uniform in $\delta$ (small enough).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The classical reference for these results is~\cite[Sections~2.7--2.9]{bahouri_fourier_2011}.
The lattice versions follow from discrete counterparts of the necessary tools
(like Young's convolution inequality).
head: environment

label: thm:besov hs norm
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:besov hs norm}
For all $\delta \geq 0$ and $f \in H^s(\Lambda_\delta)$ we have
\[
\|f\|_{H^s(\Lambda_\delta)}^2
\simeq \|(1 - \operatorname{\mathrm{\Delta}}_\delta)^{s/2} f\|_{L^2(\Lambda_\delta)}^2
\simeq \sum_{k \in \hat\Lambda_\delta} (1 + |k|^2)^s |\hat f(k)|^2.
\]
head: environment
name: Equivalent $H^s$ norm

title: Proof
body_md:
The Fourier symbols of $\Delta_j$ are bounded and only finitely many of them overlap at any point.
Both equivalences then follow from Plancherel's identity.
head: environment

label: thm:besov paraproducts
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:besov paraproducts}
The product of two smooth functions can be decomposed into two paraproducts and resonant product
\[
fg = f \prec g + f \succ g + f \odot g
\]
as in~\cite[Section~2.8]{bahouri_fourier_2011}.
We also denote $f \preceq g \coloneqq f \prec g + f \odot g$.

For any weights $\rho_1$, $\rho_2$,
and $r$, $p$, $p_1$, $p_2 \in [1, \infty]$ such that $1/p = 1/p_1 + 1/p_2$,
the paraproduct satisfies the estimate
\[
\|f \prec g\|_{B^{\min(\alpha,0) + \beta}_{p,r}(\rho_1 \rho_2)}
\lesssim \|f\|_{B^\alpha_{p_1, \infty}(\rho_1)}
    \|g\|_{B^\beta_{p_2, r}(\rho_2)},
\quad \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb R,
\]
and the resonant product satisfies
\[
\|f \odot g\|_{B^{\alpha + \beta}_{p,r}(\rho_1 \rho_2)}
\lesssim \|f\|_{B^\alpha_{p_1, \infty}(\rho_1)}
    \|g\|_{B^\beta_{p_2, r}(\rho_2)},
\quad \alpha + \beta > 0.
\]

label: def:wick
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wick}
Let $W$ be a Gaussian random variable with mean zero, and let $a = \mathord{\mathbb E} W^2$.
We define the first four Wick powers as
\[
\mathord{\mathopen: W \mathclose:} = W, \quad
\mathord{\mathopen: W^2 \mathclose:} = W^2 - a, \quad
\mathord{\mathopen: W^3 \mathclose:} = W^3 - 3 a W, \quad
\mathord{\mathopen: W^4 \mathclose:} = W^4 - 6 a W^2 + 3 a^2,
\]
and for any $\beta > 0$ we define
\[
\mathord{\mathopen: \sin(\beta W) \mathclose:} = \exp\!\left( \frac{\beta^2 a}{2} \right) \sin(\beta W), \quad
\mathord{\mathopen: \cos(\beta W) \mathclose:} = \exp\!\left( \frac{\beta^2 a}{2} \right) \cos(\beta W).
\]
head: environment
name: Wick ordering

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be centred Gaussian random variables.
Then
\[
\mathord{\mathbb E} [\mathord{\mathopen: X^n \mathclose:} \mathord{\mathopen: Y^m \mathclose:}] = n! \mathbf 1_{n=m} (\mathord{\mathbb E} [XY])^n
\]
for all $n, m \in \mathbb N$.
In particular $\mathord{\mathbb E} \mathord{\mathopen: X^n \mathclose:} = 0$ for all $n > 0$.
head: environment
name: Wick formula

label: wick-power-estimate
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{wick-power-estimate}
Let $\Lambda_\delta \subset \mathbb R^2$,
and let $W$ be distributed according to the Gaussian free field on~$\Lambda_\delta$
with mass~$m^2$.
Then for $k \in \mathbb N$ and $p < \infty$ we have
\[
\mathord{\mathbb E} \|\mathord{\mathopen: W^k \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{-\kappa}(\rho)}^p \lesssim 1 + |\log(m)|^{pk/2}.
\]
Here we assume that $\rho$ is sufficiently integrable over $\Lambda_\delta$.
head: environment
name: Moments of two-dimensional GFF

title: Proof
head: environment

label: moment-gff-sine
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{moment-gff-sine}
Let $W$ and~$\rho$ be as above, and $\beta^2 < 4\pi$.
Then
\[
\mathord{\mathbb E} \|\mathord{\mathopen: \sin(\beta W) \mathclose:}\|_{\mathcal C^{-\beta^2 / 4\pi -\kappa}(\rho)}^p
\lesssim (m\wedge1)^{-p \beta^2 / 4\pi}
\]
for sufficiently large $1 < p < \infty$. The same bound holds for the cosine.
head: environment
name: Moments of two-dimensional GFF sine

title: Proof
head: environment

label: thm:wick binomial
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:wick binomial}
Let $W$ be sampled from the Gaussian free field $\nu$,
and assume that $v \in L^{2q}(\nu;\, B^{2\varepsilon}_{pk,p}(\rho))$ for some $p, q \in [1, \infty)$
and integrable weight $\rho$.
Then
\[
\mathord{\mathopen: (W + v)^k \mathclose:} = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom k j \mathord{\mathopen: W^j \mathclose:} v^{k-j}
\]
as an element of $L^q(\nu, B^{-\varepsilon}_{p,p}(\rho^k))$.

name: Wick binomial rule

title: Proof
body_md: We only use the cases $k \leq 3$ that are computable by hand.
